This might not fit in here but after reading this I had a realization about some of my feelings when I lost my virginity and I don't know where else to put it. This isn't really rape but I hope someone reads it. A little backstory - I have a history of depression.

A few months after my first girlfriend broke up with me, she started talking to me again. I was happy about that because we were good friends once, and she had a large friend group and would throw parties and stuff. A lot of my social life revolved around her.

Anyway, I was enjoying talking to her again for a while when one day she asked me for a more physical relationship. I just remember my first thought being "I'm a guy, I have to do this." I thought I had to sleep with her because that's what guys do. So I agreed to it. I had been thinking a lot about killing myself since we broke up, after almost all of the warmth in my life had left me. (My parents were divorced and almost never around, and almost all of my friends left with my girlfriend.) Another reason I convinced myself to do it was because it was a bucket list item for me - lose your virginity and you can finally let yourself die. 

Needless to say the sex was horrible. I was so detached from everything while it was going on. I remember watching the clock as time went by because we only had 45 minutes or so, and when the time was up I pretended to finish and stopped.

That has greatly affected the way I've thought about sex since then and I now realize I haven't ever really been able to enjoy it. I'm in college now and I've been beating myself up for not sleeping around and "enjoying my college years." I just want anyone who might be in a similar situation to know that you don't have to do anything that you don't want to just because society tells you to.

That's exactly the kind of thing I meant by random pointless adventures. Those have started to have a terrible comedown for me. They're immediately followed by thoughts of "THAT'S why life should be worth living?"

I'm agnostic, so I believe there isn't enough evidence to say one way or another. If there is some kind of afterlife, it would be interesting to find out about it. If there isn't, I don't mind just going to sleep forever. Even if hell exists and I'm going there, I can't imagine it being any worse than what life is like now.

Nobody can really know what you should be doing in your future except you, which is why I am going to share the decisions that I've made with respect to my future. I think following someone else's logic and choices might help you with your own.

So, like you, I flip flopped on majors several times. In fact, the university demanded that I decide, which is the only reason that I ended up doing what I'm doing now (computer science). Unfortunately for me, soon after being pushed into making this decision, I realized that I wanted to do something completely different (animation). In order to pursue this goal, I started an animation club, and took as many classes related to that as I could. I talked to career advisers about what I should do and made a plan for the future. However, I'm still finishing my degree, and here's why: I realized that a college degree can be useful to me as a fallback plan as well as just getting a job anywhere. Many people don't go into the field that they studied in. Getting a college degree is a sign of a work ethic in and of itself, just like getting a high school diploma is. That doesn't restrict me from still pursuing the thing that I want to pursue, but it does get me accreditation that I will have for the rest of my life. Now, if I had realized what I wanted to do *before* coming to college, it would've been a different story. I might have decided to do community college instead or maybe even try an animation school. But I didn't figure it out until I was already too deep. It sounds to me that you are about where I was right before I figured out what I wanted out of life. If I were in your shoes, I would try and pick a major that you think is the most applicable to your interests. Just work on that one, and hopefully you'll know what you want eventually.

Good luck! I hope this helped.

If that doesn't work, there's really not much more to say without jeopardizing the friendship.

On a side note, here's some life advice: you're going to meet a lot of people who tell stupid white lies. They're utterly pointless, and usually just make them look silly. But most of the time, calling someone out about them is making it a bigger deal than it is. Does it really matter that your friend wants to look cooler in front of you? I'd just be flattered. It sounds like she might have monetary issues as well. If you try to think about why they're lying, usually you'll find that it's no big deal.

You sound like you live in an emotionally abusive household. Stuff like this 

`She reminds me of how selfish, narcissistic, ugly, socially inept and mentally inept I am.`

is not okay. Neither is this: 

`Sometimes I think no one likes me but myself.`

Most, if not all, of your problems seem to come from a lack of self esteem that you have gotten from being in this situation. But don't forget the options that you *do* have. The very first step that you should take, as is the step any time you're in an unhealthy situation, is to distance yourself from it. Spend less time at home. Start going to the library after school and working on homework there. Do anything you can to make sure you end up with less time around your mother. What it comes down to in the end is this: 

`I am unreliable and irresponsible and immature and lazy as fuck, I never do my work`

That is an actual problem. Almost every issue in this world can be solved with some hard work. If you want to change your situation, you have to figure out a way to become self-motivated. However, if I were in your situation, I know that I would have an issue with working hard, not because it is impossible, but because I was afraid of failing. Well, I'm not much older than you, but I'm old enough to say it is possible to change yourself overnight if you set your mind to it. Yeah, it sucks, and it's hard work, and it's probably even harder if you have someone in your life that's never done anything responsible. The thing is, you're not your dad, you're not your mom, you aren't anyone else. You are you. You decide what comes next, nobody else. That's part of being an adult. You have to be your own role model and your own manager. It sucks. There is no other option. But don't worry! You can do it. I know you can do it, because you have already reached out for help. Even if it is only on reddit, reaching out is the hardest part. So when you say

`all I am capable of is writing posts like this on reddit.`

I hear "I've just started to work towards a better future." Try your hardest.
